messages:
Sam Liu: FYI nightly bench looks noisy — p99 spiked ~18% after the attn-kernel switch + quant-optim PR. Not visible in median.
Maria Chen: ugh thanks for flagging. which job? link?
Sam Liu: bench-bot: https://ci.redwood.example/jobs/6221 run 2026-03-12 02:10Z. Summary:
```
model: redwood/attn-v2
variant: q4_0
seq_distribution: {short: 60%, mid: 30%, long: 10%}
throughput_med: 1020 tok/s
p99_latency: 310ms (prev: 262ms)
```
Maria Chen: interesting — throughput stable, tail up. Could be a scheduling/fallback for long sequences or quantized kernel edge-case.
Cheng Park: did we change kernel selector ordering? the new selector prefers fused-attn when seq>=128 and q4 quant. that could trigger a slower codepath under specific shapes.
Sam Liu: yes the selector change landed in PR #4120 last week. It added a tie-breaker that biases toward fused when memory_headroom < 0.25.
Jordan Patel: quick thought: our sample mix is skewed towards short prefix but long completion in real traffic. Nightly harness uses synthetic seeds that produce uniform completions — sampling mismatch might hide these edges.
Maria Chen: can you paste the bench invocation?
Sam Liu: `./bench_harness --model redwood/attn-v2 --variant q4_0 --seed 42 --seq-shape-mix 60,30,10 --clients 8 --request-size 512`
Oliver Martinez: I notice in the run logs we see occasional "kernel_fallback_to_generic" events correlated with p99s. snippet:
```
[02:10:45] WARN kernel_selector: fused_attn failed init, fallback: generic_attn (reason: kernel_workspace_alloc_fail)
[02:10:45] INFO kvcache: miss 12/120
[02:10:46] METRIC latency p99 318ms
```
Cheng Park: that fallback could explain 90-120ms outliers. why would workspace allocation fail only after selector change? maybe fused_attn has higher temporary workspace at certain R and head dims.
Maria Chen: also quantization path for q4_0 uses different kernel code; combined with fused attn might increase peak memory and cause intermittent OOM during workspace alloc.
Jordan Patel: hypothesis: the harness sampling has long sequences but not mixed prefixes, so KV cache warmup patterns differ. Suggest two experiments: 1) reproduce with deterministic real-trace replay; 2) run stratified microbench with fine-grained seq/head dims to find shape trigger.
Sam Liu: +1. I can run a repro: `./bench_harness --replay-trace s3://bench-traces/2026-03-10/real-traffic-1k.json --variant q4_0 --clients 16`
bench-bot: job queued — https://ci.redwood.example/jobs/6223 (replay-run)
Maria Chen: while that's running, propose a small harness change: emit per-request kernel selection tag in telemetry and a small experiment to weight our sampling by observed production seq_len distribution. That will make nightly more predictive.
Oliver Martinez: good. Also add an assertion in harness: if fallback_count > 0 and p99 delta > 10% then fail the run and attach logs. Currently we only fail on throughput drops.
Cheng Park: careful — some fallbacks are expected on older GPUs. But tagging them and failing only when correlated with latency regression sounds safe.
Sam Liu: I'll open a PR that: 1) records `selector_choice` per request, 2) stratifies sample mix by live-percentiles, 3) adds fallback->latency correlation assertion. Draft PR #4190.
Maria Chen: can you also dump device free memory right before kernel init in the fused_attn path when fallback happens? that should prove workspace pressure cause.
Sam Liu: will add logs.
Jordan Patel: test matrix to run: q4_0 + fused_attn selector on A100/MI250, seq shapes: 64/128/256, batch 1/4/8, replay vs synthetic. I'll coordinate infra slots.
Maria Chen: TL;DR action items: Sam -> repro + PR for harness telemetry & guard. Cheng -> audit fused_attn workspace sizing vs quant kernels. Oliver -> add run-fail rule. Jordan -> schedule test matrix. I'll follow up in this thread with the PR link and job results. :thumbsup:
Oliver Martinez: thanks. ping me when PR is up, I'll review fast.
bench-bot: job 6223 finished: https://ci.redwood.example/jobs/6223 — p99 back to baseline on replay but two fallback events logged (see artifacts).
